lesson_title: How Many Muffins Before You Stop Losing Money?
hook_text: You've baked 80 muffins. How many do you actually have to sell before you stop losing money?
clip_script: Two columns. Fixed costs, the same whatever you sell: table R50, posters R30, gas R40. R120. Variable costs, growing with every muffin: ingredients and cups, R3,50 each. Total for 80: R400. Cost price: R5 a muffin. Sell at R10. Now the magic number: each muffin gives R6,50 towards the fixed costs. R120 divided by R6,50: about 19. Sell 19 and you've broken even. Every muffin after that is profit. Market day: 72 sold, last 8 at R6, still above cost. Sold out. That is an Entrepreneur's Day budget.
visual_style: A whiteboard two-column cost list, a muffin counter ticking up to 19 with a break-even flag, then a profit stack.
mood: Practical and suspenseful, a numbers countdown.
pacing: Quick cost build, a dramatic break-even reveal, then a market-day finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work out the break-even point for your own stall idea.
